Out of scope: the rest of REQ-06-02 (the notch calculator itself), Ind. 11-13, any UI, CLI or printed output, ratings outside the 19-step scale (for example CC, C, D, NR, which are rejected as unknown), and other rating-agency scales or outlooks/watches.

items.answer: The request supports testable criteria with concrete values. REQ-06-02 gives notchChange('BBB+','BB+') === 3, notchChange('BB+','BBB+') === -3 and notchChange('A','A') === 0. C1 gives the scale, trimming and case-insensitivity ('bbb+' equals 'BBB+'). C2 gives the RangeError cases (unknown rating, '', non-string, new String('A')). C3 gives the sign. Boundaries can be derived from the scale: notchChange('AAA','CCC-') === 18 and notchChange('CCC-','AAA') === -18.
items.quote: BBB+ → BB+ = 3-notch downgrade

items.answer: There are no contradictions. The examples match C1 and C3: BBB+ is index 7 and BB+ is index 10, so the change is +3 (downgrade positive), the reverse is -3, and A to A is 0. The scale has exactly 19 entries, as the request states. One wording point: 'next to the code under test/' could mean a test file beside src/ratings/notch.mjs. The request itself says 'under test/', and the repo convention is test/<area>/<name>.test.mjs, so the test file is test/ratings/notch.test.mjs.

items.answer: Module: src/ratings/notch.mjs, ES module, named exports. (1) RATING_SCALE holds the 19 ratings in this order: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-. These are upper-case ASCII strings with an ASCII hyphen-minus, best first. Its exact JS shape and mutability are in X-scale-shape. (2) notchChange(previous, current) returns a Number integer equal to index(current) - index(previous) on the scale. A downgrade is positive, an upgrade is negative, and no change is 0. The range is -18..18. Each argument must be a primitive string. It is trimmed with String.prototype.trim() and compared case-insensitively. Null, undefined, empty and non-string arguments are covered by C2 and CON-errors.
items.quote: The result is signed: downgrade positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0.

items.answer: Every invalid argument throws a RangeError, never a TypeError and never a return value. This covers: an unknown rating ('D', 'BBB +', 'AAA-'); an empty string ''; a string that is empty after trim ('   '); and any non-string, which includes undefined (a missing argument), null, numbers, booleans, objects, arrays, Symbols and boxed strings such as new String('A'). The type is checked before trim(), so Symbol and null cannot cause a TypeError. If either argument is invalid, the call throws. The message text is not specified (see X-error-message).
items.quote: Every invalid input (an unknown rating, an empty string, a non-string) is rejected with a RangeError.

items.answer: RATING_SCALE is a frozen Array (Object.freeze) of the 19 strings, best first
items.source: pm: michael 2026-10-05 — the request says 'best first', which implies an ordered list, and freezing stops a consumer from corrupting the order notchChange relies on
items.question: What exact JS shape and mutability should RATING_SCALE have? The request says only 'the 19 ratings of C1, best first'.
options: A frozen Array of 19 strings (Object.freeze), so consumers cannot change the order notchChange relies on (recommended)
Another structure, such as a Map from rating to index (not recommended: the request says 'best first', which implies an ordered list)
items.impact: With a frozen array, consumer mutation fails silently in sloppy mode or throws in strict mode, and notchChange cannot be corrupted. A mutable array lets one consumer break every other caller.
